chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that 'Ali, peace be upon him, used to say:
There is no amputation upon the thief until he takes the stolen property out of the house, and it is of the amount for which amputation becomes obligatory.

key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief who commits the act of theft
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the house or enclosed place from which the property is stolen
key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: the hadd punishment of amputation prescribed for qualifying theft
key_terms.بِالسَّرِقَةِ: with the stolen property taken by theft

ai.seo_question: When does the hadd punishment for theft apply in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal condition for the hadd punishment of theft: the stolen property must actually be removed from the house, and it must reach the qualifying amount that necessitates amputation. It reflects the precision of Islamic jurisprudence in restricting penal punishments to cases that fulfill specific legal criteria.
